native_result.query: In which domain do the majority of authors tend to be male for both original and replication studies?
native_result.HypoA: In Experimental Economics, the majority of authors tend to be male for both original and replication studies with ratio of males in original and replication studies being and 0.87 and 0.84 respectively.
native_result.HypoB: Economics is the domain in which the majority of authors tend to be male for both original and replication studies: 10 of 18 Economics O/R pairs (55.6%) have authors_male.o > 0.5 and authors_male.r > 0.5 (strict criterion), the highest share versus Cognitive (18/49 = 36.7%) and Social (20/74 = 27.0%), and Economics also shows the highest mean male-author ratios for both original (0.870) and replication (0.837) studies. The Economics > Cognitive > Social ranking held under both sensitivity variants (row-level unit and inclusive >= 0.5 threshold). Caveat: Economics rests on only 18 pairs, so its estimate is less precise than the other domains.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded the primary dataset (927 rows, 141 unique O/R pairs). Defined majority-male-in-both as authors_male.o > 0.5 AND authors_male.r > 0.5 at O/R-pair level, with each multi-lab (ml1/ml3) pair's replication ratio taken as the mean of its lab rows. Computed per-discipline share and counts of qualifying pairs plus mean ratios, then ran two sensitivity variants: (a) row-level unit (each lab replication counted) and (b) inclusive >= 0.5 threshold. Economics led on all metrics in all variants; exact counts/percentages and Wilson 95% CI computed; no missing values required handling.

sub_hypo.text: In Experimental Economics, the majority of authors are male in both original and replication studies, with male author ratios of 0.87 and 0.84, respectively.
sub_hypo.context: Original and replication studies in Experimental Economics.
sub_hypo.relations: Male authors constitute a majority in both original and replication studies, with ratios of 0.87 in original studies and 0.84 in replication studies.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: In Experimental Economics, the majority of authors tend to be male for both original and replication studies with ratio of males in original and replication studies being and 0.87 and 0.84 respectively.

sub_hypo.text: Economics has the highest share of original/replication pairs with a strict majority of male authors in both studies: 10/18 (55.6%), compared with Cognitive at 18/49 (36.7%) and Social at 20/74 (27.0%).
sub_hypo.context: Primary dataset of 927 rows and 141 unique original/replication pairs, analyzed at pair level. For multi-lab ml1/ml3 pairs, the replication male-author ratio is averaged across lab rows. Economics has only 18 pairs, making its estimate less precise than those of the other domains; Wilson 95% confidence intervals were computed.
sub_hypo.relations: The share satisfying authors_male.o > 0.5 AND authors_male.r > 0.5 ranks Economics (55.6%) > Cognitive (36.7%) > Social (27.0%).

sub_hypo.text: Economics has the highest mean male-author ratios for both original studies (0.870) and replication studies (0.837).
sub_hypo.context: Original/replication pairs in the primary dataset, grouped by Economics, Cognitive, and Social disciplines; replication ratios for multi-lab ml1/ml3 pairs are averaged across lab rows before pair-level analysis.
sub_hypo.relations: Mean authors_male.o and mean authors_male.r are both highest in Economics.

sub_hypo.text: The Economics > Cognitive > Social ranking in the share with majority-male authors in both studies persists under row-level analysis and an inclusive majority threshold; Economics also leads on mean male-author ratios in all variants.
sub_hypo.context: Two sensitivity variants of the primary dataset analysis: counting each lab replication as a row-level unit, and replacing the strict > 0.5 threshold with an inclusive >= 0.5 threshold.
sub_hypo.relations: The share ranking Economics > Cognitive > Social persists when each lab replication is counted separately and when qualification requires authors_male.o >= 0.5 AND authors_male.r >= 0.5. Economics retains the highest mean male-author ratios for both original and replication studies.

gen_sub_hypo.full_hypo: Economics is the domain in which the majority of authors tend to be male for both original and replication studies: 10 of 18 Economics O/R pairs (55.6%) have authors_male.o > 0.5 and authors_male.r > 0.5 (strict criterion), the highest share versus Cognitive (18/49 = 36.7%) and Social (20/74 = 27.0%), and Economics also shows the highest mean male-author ratios for both original (0.870) and replication (0.837) studies. The Economics > Cognitive > Social ranking held under both sensitivity variants (row-level unit and inclusive >= 0.5 threshold). Caveat: Economics rests on only 18 pairs, so its estimate is less precise than the other domains.
